utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I do not know exactly what the status in e-court of this document is because it's not part of the admitted transcripts. If I try to open it for myself, access is denied. That may be a technical problem, but do you want to tender it then?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to Your Honour's guide-lines, we plan to review what we used at the end of the day and maybe only tender the portions we used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not the whole -- not the whole transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay that's fine as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because I uploaded it seven days ago and I wasn't sure at that time what I'm going to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perfectly clear. Perfectly acceptable. The reason why I'm asking it is if you put to the witness: Is your answer accurate? And if we have not read what the answer was, then of course we would not know what the evidence is unless we have those portions in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore it is also important that you always clearly refer to on what page we are so that it's -- that we are better able to find it. Please proceed and take care of this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will try to cure my mistake. Can we have 1D411, page 15, on the screen, please, lines 19 to 24, please. That's regarding the take-over of power and that family of Mr. Mirza Mujadzic left Prijedor was on the next page, page 16, and transcript page 6790, from rows 4 to row 6 line section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. What I specifically referred to was page 45, lines 7 and following, where you say you were asked whether, et cetera, et cetera, and then without saying whether he -- whether the witness confirmed or denied the accuracy you asked is that piece of information correct, where you were only referring to the question whether or not. So we do not know whether he confirmed or not, but we'll find that in the transcript of the other case. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regarding that information I can give you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you put to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- information he said, he confirmed it to be correct. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can find it at page 9, lines 11 to 13 [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that's of course why I insisted so much in having it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to have page 31 from this document -- actually 414. I need 1D414, page 31. Page 31, please. Yes, transcript page number 13209. Line 16. I will read in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will quote from English transcript. Mr. Sivac was recorded to say: "The Omarska camp as well ... all of the other camps in Prijedor were established by the civilian authorities of the municipality of Prijedor." Then he talks about Mr. Milan Andzic who provided logistics. Now we need next page, line 4 to 7. So it's page 32. Question was, I quote: "And the civilian authority you're referring to is the Prijedor Crisis Staff; is that right? "A. Yes. Civilian authorities headed by the Crisis Staff of the municipality."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sivac, would you say the same today, that the camps in Prijedor had been set up by the Prijedor civilian authorities headed by the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked about armed groups from Kozarac, Hambarine, and I am also going to ask you whether it is true that the aim of these armed groups was to breakthrough towards Bihac, carrying out smaller attacks on the VRS en route?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was their plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let me ask you this, it concerns Milomir Stakic. At the trial of Milomir Stakic you claim to have recognised him in the Omarska camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you make the same claim today?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also when you spoke about -- just a moment, please. When you spoke about the visit of the delegation to Omarska, you mentioned some other people who were present there. And we need 1D410 in e-court, page 38, lines 22 to 24. Here you enumerated the names of the people you recognised, and in line 23 you say Zivko Ecim, Rade Mutic, Ostoja Kesar, Slobodan Pesevic, and Boro Maric. Then there are some additional names which is on page 6741 of the Stakic trial on 31st July 2002, and then there are some names in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the transcript number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you repeat the transcript number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it the page of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 6741 was the previous page number, and now we need 6743.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And there you say the politicians in the delegation were Radoslav Brdjanin, Vojo Kupresanin, Dr. Radislav Vukic. From Prijedor were present Simo Miskovic, Milomir Stakic, Srdjo Srdic, Simo Drljaca. Did you recognise these people when they came to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. May I address the President because I have a problem. Mr. President, I have a small problem. I to leave the courtroom for a minute. I do apologise, but it's force majeure and I have some health issues. I'll be back shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We might use the time for other purposes at this moment. In relation to Witness RM511 I think there were two requests. One we have dealt with already, that is the chart to be used for identification of voices in audio records, intercepts, but there was also a request to use with Witness RM511 a chart in relation to documents. Mr. Lukic, I think we have not heard yet the position of the Defence in relation to the use of these documents through this chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Stojanovic is dealing with the next witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- and I think he will address you on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you tell us whether there's any objection to the proposed course?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we are talking about the same thing, we received today a table of abbreviations and terms to be used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, what -- no. What I'm talking about is a list of 16 documents to be used with RM511 and the chart which is intended to seek the comments regarding the authenticity of those 16 documents and any comments on the substance of those documents. The question is whether the Defence would agree with the use of these documents through this chart?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Yesterday we talked to our client at the Detention Unit and I think that it is acceptable for these documents to be used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and also for the chart to be used, but then later we'll find entries by this witness on authenticity and the substance of the documents, at least comments on that. Then under those circumstances, Mr. Groome, the Chamber allows you to proceed as you suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might usefully or make use of this time until the witness returns, the other document that Mr. Stojanovic referred to is a document that I provided the Defence earlier, and in preparing for 511 it occurred to me that -- how important it is to be precise about the use of language and words B/C/S don't always translate precisely into English. So what I've proposed is a demonstrative exhibit which takes -- will be an exhibit in this case, it is the official lexicon of the JNA army which defines all of the terms, and to turn that into an exhibit that we all can use so that we can be precise in the language we use and that there's no confusion in the use of military terms. For example, there are two B/C/S words for the -- that translate into the word "order," so to ensure that we are using it precisely I've offered the Defence to add any additional words that they think will be useful and hopefully that process will be completed before Monday and we'll be able to be distribute that to the Chamber. And I see the witness is returning to the Chamber, so I'll sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise to the Chamber and to you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No need to apologise. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When I listed the names of the Banja Luka politicians, I mentioned Radoslav Brdjanin, Vojo Kupresanin, Dr. Radislav Vukic. Did you see all of them in Omarska on that day?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vukic, Brdjanin, no, I didn't Kupresanin but I saw --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last two names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- you said you didn't see Kupresanin, but you did see ... and then repeat those names, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stojan Zupljanin and Predrag Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what you said in the Stakic trial that you saw Vojo Kupresanin is not correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct. I used to mix up Zupljanin and Kupresanin. I thought that they had similar faces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D405 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, this is your statement of 12 to 16 November 1994. We're still waiting for it to appear on the screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Very briefly, Your Honours, if I may just refer back to the document Mr. Lukic was quoting from, the prior transcript, it may be that Mr. Lukic was, in fact, asking this witness a question by reading from this witness statement, and that appears to be what it was rather than the witness's testimony in the Stakic case. But I'll let Mr. Lukic clarify if needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please verify, Mr. Lukic, and see whether there's any need to adjust what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can go back to that, but I was reading from the transcript from Stakic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that that was not the issue but who was speaking or who -- Mr. Shin, that seems to be the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I was just going to that page 6741 in the Stakic testimony where Mr. Lukic's question begins at line 13, indicating that he is reading -- I'm sorry, I'm speaking too quickly. I'll slow down. That Mr. Lukic indicates that he is reading the whole paragraph, and if we return to page 6740, in line 19 we see that that is, in fact, the paragraph from the witness statement that we have just now have on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'd say it was -- the transcript does not reflect what the witness testified but was reflecting what his statement contained?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. It appears to be that Mr. Lukic was reading from this statement which is currently on the screen in order to put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are in a position to verify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From this statement I need page 24 in B/C/S or page 34 in English version. Can I see ERN number in B/C/S version because I don't think that's the page, please. You have to go one page back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the second paragraph in the middle towards the end of line it reads that among the politicians were Radoslav Brdjanin, Vojo Kupresanin, Dr. Radislav Vukic. Do you recall making this statement in November 1994?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But it's incorrect with regard to Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you, I used to confuse Zupljanin and Kupresanin. I didn't know them very well and hence the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you testified in the Zupljanin case you said that it was not Kupresanin but that it was, in fact, him who you saw?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was him, Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 1D410 in e-court. We need page 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the Stakic case on transcript page 6753 I ask you this in line 14 - I'll read it out in English. [In English] "Q. What was the role of the army in the running of the Omarska camp? "A. I don't know what the chain of command was. I'm not familiar with that. But as a prisoner, I had the impression that they didn't have any business connections with the camp. In the Omarska camp, as well as Trnopolje and Keraterm, there were no soldiers, and that's why I think that the army did not have any authority over these camps and that they were run by the civilian authorities of Prijedor Municipality." [Interpretation] When you testified back then, did you tell the truth, Mr. Sivac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. As for any subordination that existed between the military and police structures, at the time it was unclear to me. And any kind of co-ordination or manning mechanisms they had in place, I only learned about that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll go back to one sentence which I read a moment ago in order to put a specific question. [In English] "In the Omarska camp, as well as Trnopolje and Keraterm, there were no soldiers, and that's why I think that the army did not have any authority over these camps ..." [Interpretation] Would you agree today that as a detainee you did not see a single soldier?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be incorrect. In my previous statements and testimony before this Court, I identified all such soldiers who were members of the city battalion stationed around the Trnopolje camp. I can reiterate that today if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So when you testified in the Stakic case, you did not tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you believe. It's an assertion of yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether what you said in the Stakic case is true or not. You tell me.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said then is what I repeat now. I told the truth about my initial impression. I -- as far as I remember I mentioned soldiers in all of my statements. I knew many of them. Some of them had been my friends. There's nothing else I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mico Kovacevic in the Omarska camp who was the then-Municipal Assembly speaker of Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. It was when the political delegation came.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have Exhibit 1D407 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is your statement of the 30th of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the ERN number in the English -- sorry, in the B/C/S version. There seems to be something wrong with the ERN numbers. Does this statement have two 7s as the last two digits on any of the pages? Could we go to the last page, please. [In English] My version is obviously different from this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, perhaps a matter to be sorted out during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us how much more time you would need because I think you used now close to two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Five minutes. After the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: After you've sorted out your things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would the next witness be available, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. He's just outside the door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break and we'll -- after the witness has left the courtroom, and could the usher escort him out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, could you already give us an indication as to how much time you would need for re-examination as matters stand now?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. If there is to be any redirect at all, it will be less than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means we would have approximately half an hour left for the next witness. We'll take a break and we'll resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While the witness is entering --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While the witness is brought in -- I sorted out my papers and we will need 1D407 on the screen, first pages and then we'll move just for witness to see that it's his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, you can see your statement on the screen in front of you given on the 30th of March, 1998. We need page 4 in the English middle of the page and page 6 in the B/C/S version, bottom of the page. In this statement which you gave to the Tribunal officials there's a paragraph in the B/C/S then a single line where you say: "I never saw Kovacevic in Omarska."

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't see my signature anywhere here. This is a bit puzzling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's -- at least in the English version, and I'm checking at this moment about the B/C/S version, but I find no signatures yet. I find in -- in neither version I find any signatures, not to say that you still can ask the witness whether he recognises this as his statement, but he might need more time to go through it. Of course I'm also looking in the direction of the Prosecution. This apparently is a witness statement taken by investigators of the OTP. Mr. Shin -- and I noticed another thing before I give you an opportunity to respond. In the English version at the bottom it says on the -- what seems to be the last page in e-court, it says "page 6 of 7," therefore you would expect another page, and of course we couldn't exclude that a signature is found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. I think we're good. Yes, Your Honours, I'm informed that we do not have a signed version of this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, which requires then great caution, Mr. Lukic, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, do you remember that this statement was used during your testimony in the Stakic case?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me when I say I don't. I also don't remember this statement of mine. I have provided many statements and I have been visited by a number of investigation teams, including some people from the country where I resided at the time. So I really can't recall off-the-cuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go back to our previous topic then. Is it correct that you have never in any statement or testimony before this one said that in Omarska and Keraterm there were any soldiers. And if you believe you have said something to that effect, do indicate it to us.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you this, Mr. Lukic: As regards Trnopolje, when you asked me about that, I understood your question. I can't recall exactly. I think you asked me who was in charge of the Trnopolje camp and I said civilian authorities, and indeed they were. But no one asked me who provided security in the Trnopolje camp. And in all of my statements thus far I mentioned Slobodan Kuruzovic and Boro Grubic and Zoran Knegenic [phoen]. They were all members of the city battalion or the town battalion of the VRS, so it may have been a misunderstanding. The way I understood the question was who officially established the Omarska and Trnopolje camps. They were created by decisions of the Crisis Staff which was a civilian body. It's another issue who provided security for the camps. I guess I made a switch there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 6753 in the Stakic case, you said there were no soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have misspoken or perhaps you should keep listening to my testimony and I think you'll find that I mentioned Slobodan Kuruzovic and all those soldiers who guarded us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Kuruzovic, the Balaban brothers, and members of the town brigade, that was with regards to Trnopolje; correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not with regards to Omarska and Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They guarded the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sivac. That would be all and I would like to thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to thank you as well for being fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, simply two questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I could please ask the Court Officer to pull up P480 and turn to page -- I'll wait until it's up. And turn to page 39 in the e-court which would be transcript 6627.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Sivac, Counsel Lukic has just asked you about soldiers in Omarska, and I will read you very briefly from your testimony in the Stakic case. You are responding here to a question from the Prosecution, and if I -- I'm sorry, if I go to the previous page, page 38 and transcript page 6626. The question Prosecution counsel has asked you then is "were you" -- I'm sorry, I'll repeat that. Quote: "And were you then taken to the area of Omarska known as the garage?" And part of your answer, if I may just skip to this part of P480, now back to page 39, 6627 of the transcript, on lines 3 through 8 -- I'm sorry, 3 through 10. You state: "And close to the iron door in one of the corners of the garage, Professor Muhamed Cehajic, president of Prijedor Municipality, was lying all alone. He had obviously been beaten severely. You could see that he had been maltreated. He urinated blood. I will never forget that night. Around 8.00 in the evening, the door slammed open, and a Serb soldier appeared. He was wearing red shades. He began to yell and threaten us. He cocked his weapon. Behind him, there were the other guards standing." Mr. Sivac, do you stand by your answer that I have just read out in your Stakic testimony?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Sivac, you have mentioned in the delegation visit to -- in response to questions both from me and Mr. Lukic, you mentioned that in the delegation visit to Omarska while you were a detainee there that one of the persons present there was Radmilo Zeljaja. Can you please tell us whether you stand by that answer and who Radmilo Zeljaja was by position?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SIVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. He was the commander of the 43rd Motorised Brigade of the VRS from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shin. The Bench has no further questions. Mr. Lukic, you have no further questions. Mr. Sivac, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for answering all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, for having listened to what I had to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Protective measures for the next witness would be face distortion and pseudonym which requires that when the witness enters the courtroom that the curtains should be down and that the screens should be in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll take this opportunity just to rearrange our staff as well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the curtains be drawn up again. I take it that face distortion is in place? It is. Good afternoon, Witness RM110. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you and I would like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Witness, we'll not call you by your own name. We will call you Witness RM110. And your face is also not visible for those outside this courtroom. You will first be examined by Ms. Hochhauser. Ms. Hochhauser is counsel for the Prosecution. Ms. Hochhauser, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. I do have a fairly detailed record of the adjudicated facts, but -- which I didn't get to make, but I would suggest if it's all right doing it once the witness leaves the courtroom today since we won't get through the rest of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you'd postpone that. That's -- okay, let's start with the witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because we have limited time left and otherwise he might feel to be superfluous which he is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 28484 on the monitor, not to be displayed outside of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us, please, whether you recognise your own name and date of birth on that sheet?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if I might tender this into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28484 becomes Exhibit P490 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P490 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Witness, you have given statements to the Office of the Prosecutor previously on the 22nd February 1996 and the 11th of March, 1997, as well as testified previously in cases against Dragomir Milosevic, Momcilo Perisic, and Radovan Karadzic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And if we could please have 65 ter 28483, again not to be broadcast outside of the courtroom on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise what is being displayed on the monitor in front of you to be one of the witness statements that you signed on 22nd February 1996?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of the statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: In preparation for your testimony in the Karadzic case, on the 1st of November, 2010, you signed a statement which amalgamated some relevant portions of your previous OTP statements and your testimony up until that point; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser, would you switch off your microphone if --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the witness answers. I may have made a mistake. There's no voice distortion, there's only face distortion, so therefore apologies for my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So, sir, I just asked you about the preparation of an amalgamated statement before your Karadzic testimony. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I could please have 65 ter 28482 on the monitor, again not to be displayed outside of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise what is now on the monitor as the 2010 amalgamated statement that we just discussed?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise my signature at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, with regard to both of these statements that we've now seen on the monitor assigned 65 ter numbers 28482 and 28483, did you have the opportunity to review them again before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And is there anything in either of those statements that you would like to change or correct?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: No, there isn't anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If asked the same questions today that you were asked when providing the information contained in those two statements, would you give the same answers today?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And is all the information in both of those statements truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes, they are truthful and accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I now tender under seal both 65 ter number 28482 and 28483 along with the associated exhibits, as indicated on the revised exhibit list provided to the Defence and Chamber. I would note that in terms of the associated exhibits, Your Honour -- I'm sorry, if you would just give me one second -- I apologise. I'm offering the -- along with the associated exhibits as indicated on the revised exhibit list provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's start with the two statements. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28483 becomes Exhibit P491, Your Honours. And document 28482 becomes Exhibit P492, Your Honours, both under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Both are admitted under seal. Now, as far as the associated exhibits are concerned, Ms. Hochhauser, we received the list and let's just see whether that's the most recent one. I -- yes. The first one I think is 10046; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Official report. Any objections? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10046 becomes Exhibit P493, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence under seal. The next one would be, Ms. Hochhauser, shaded items not -- would that mean that 10121 is the next one?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P494, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next one would be 10134 -- by the way, for P494 I should have said "under seal." Then 10134 is the next one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P495, Your Honours, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted under seal. Next one, 10234.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P496, Your Honours, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might address the last one of the associated exhibits which is 65 ter number 13865. I'll make a more detailed record of it later, but in reliance on adjudicated facts I will not be tendering that at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then 10352, does that remain?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: No, Judge, that should be shaded on the chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should be shaded. And 12844 --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also. So we have dealt with all those you wanted to tender. Mr. Stojanovic, I carefully looked at you but I always noticed that there were no objections against these documents. Please proceed, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could at this time read the public summary of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So RM110 worked for the Sarajevo security services from around April of 1994 until the end of the conflict. In this role, RM110 participated in the investigation of numerous shelling and sniping incidents. RM110 was often on the site of investigations and recorded many of others' conclusions and observations as well as his own in official reports. Among other investigations, RM110 investigated four scheduled incidents, including F-11, the firing on passengers on a tram on 8 October 1994; G-13, the use of a modified air bomb on Safeta Hadzica Street on 26 May 1994; and G-18, the shelling of the Markale Market on 28 August 1995. And I notice that I believe I misspoke. I should have said "three scheduled incidents." The written evidence of RM110 also covers the investigation of unscheduled shelling incidents both from 28 June of 1995, one, the bombing of the TV building; and second, the bombing of Geteova Street number 5 in the Alipasino Polje neighbourhood; as well as an unscheduled sniping incident on 14th of May, 1995, in which Jasmina Tabakovic was killed in her bedroom in Dobrinja. In each instance, the on-site investigation identified the origin of fire as Bosnian Serb-held territory. That concludes the summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have further questions for the witness, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, RM110, as you know, the Chamber's already in possession of your statements, the statements that you've just seen that have been on the monitor. And so as a result, I'm going to limit my questions to either clarifying information in those statements or eliciting information that is not contained in them. So in regard to what is now in evidence as P493 under seal, and that is the shooting incident at a tram, incident F-11, on 8 October 1994, in that exhibit at -- in the English page 2 and the bottom of page 1 in the B/C/S, the weapon that is -- the report describes the weapon used as a death sower. Can you tell us what is meant by a death sower? And this -- this is an exhibit that's under seal.

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Well, that's what I heard from my colleagues who were a ballistics expert, that it involved fire-arm with a long barrel and that can fire a large amount of rounds. So usually people say that anyone who has this kind of gun pointed at them due to speedy fire is unable to flee and avoid consequences, and for that reason it was named death sower.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now I'm going to turn now to the event on 26 May 1995 on Safeta Hadzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can we please have 656 ter 10132 on the screen and this is a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you have the opportunity to look through this series of photographs prior to coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And are they accurately identified as coming from the scene of Safeta Hadzica Street on 26 May 1995?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes. As far as the photographs that I saw are concerned, this is the scene on Safeta Hadzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And were you present at that scene?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And do the photographs accurately depict the location as you saw it after the bombing?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: At the moment I can see only one photo, but what I saw before I appeared in court, yes, the photographs were taken at that location where projectiles landed on Safeta Hadzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, at this time I'd like to tender 65 ter 10132 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10132 becomes Exhibit P497, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence as a public exhibit. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now if we could please have Exhibit 495 under seal on the monitor -- oh, I apologise, P495.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And I'd like to just quickly draw your attention at page 5 in the English and page 6 in the B/C/S, and in the B/C/S I believe it's the third full paragraph from the bottom, second sentence of that paragraph. And it indicates there that the explosion was in front of number 52, whereas elsewhere in the report it indicates -- it states number 152. I believe you've addressed this at previous testimony, but is it -- are those two separate incidents or is it a typographical error?

utterances.speaker: RM110
utterances.text: No, that's one and the same incident. Probably the error occurred during the typing of this report, and I'm referring to the error in the number. If I remember correctly, at the moment the number should be 52.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now if we could go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at the same time I'm looking at the clock. We have to finish in one minute from now. I don't know whether it's worthwhile to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: No, it's not, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Witness RM110, I'd like to instruct you, because we'll adjourn for the day, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in any other way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given already today or whether that is testimony still to be given next week. If that's clear to you, you may follow the usher and we'd like to see you back on Monday morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser, I think reading the relevant adjudicated facts could be best done when we are waiting for the witness to enter the courtroom on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That usually takes close to a minute before the witness is there, rather than to ask for further patience of interpreters, security, and transcribers. We adjourn for the day and we will resume Monday, the 12th of November, at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, III.
